extra.message: The user-controlled 'orderBy' query parameter (SearchParameters.getOrderBy()) is concatenated directly into the SQL string ('... order by ' + orderBy) and is only checked by ColumnValidator.validateSqlInjection(). That validator is regex/blacklist based and does not detect bare subqueries (the documented ZDRES-035 ColumnValidator bypass): payloads such as '(SELECT SLEEP(3))' or 'id, (select password from m_appuser limit 1)-- -' contain no semicolon, no AND/OR and no comparison operator, so getOperand() returns an empty set and validation passes. The injected ORDER BY expression is then executed by the database, allowing time-based blind/data-exfiltration SQL injection via GET /v1/loans.

User-controlled 'orderBy' is concatenated into the SQL executed for the savings-account listing ('... order by ' + searchParameters.getOrderBy()) and guarded only by the bypassable ColumnValidator.validateSqlInjection(). A payload such as '(SELECT SLEEP(3))' passes validation and is executed, yielding time-based blind SQL injection. Same ZDRES-035 ColumnValidator subquery bypass class that was fixed for offices/clients/centers but not here.

The non-paged group listing appends the user-controlled 'orderBy'/'sortOrder' values directly into the SQL ('order by ' + searchParameters.getOrderBy() + ' ' + searchParameters.getSortOrder()) and validates them only with ColumnValidator.validateSqlInjection(), whose blacklist regex misses bare subqueries. An attacker can inject an arbitrary ORDER BY expression such as '(SELECT SLEEP(5))', enabling blind SQL injection via GET /v1/groups.

The journal-entry listing concatenates the user-controlled 'orderBy'/'sortOrder' request parameters into the SQL string and relies on ColumnValidator.validateSqlInjection(), which does not block subquery ORDER BY payloads. This permits SQL injection (e.g. time-based '(SELECT SLEEP(5))' or data extraction) through the journal entries API.

Account-transfer listing concatenates user-controlled 'orderBy'/'sortOrder' directly into SQL and validates only with the bypassable ColumnValidator.validateSqlInjection(). Bare subqueries in ORDER BY are not detected, allowing blind SQL injection through the account transfers endpoints.

Standing-instruction listing appends the user-supplied 'orderBy'/'sortOrder' values into the SQL statement and validates them with ColumnValidator.validateSqlInjection(), which is bypassable by subquery payloads (ZDRES-035). This allows SQL injection via the standing instructions API.

SMS message listing concatenates the user-controlled 'orderBy'/'sortOrder' values into SQL and validates with ColumnValidator.validateSqlInjection(), which does not catch bare subqueries in ORDER BY. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL expressions, enabling blind SQL injection via the SMS API.

Deposit-account on-hold transaction listing concatenates user-controlled 'orderBy'/'sortOrder' parameters into the SQL and validates with the bypassable ColumnValidator.validateSqlInjection(). Subquery ORDER BY payloads such as '(SELECT SLEEP(3))' pass validation and execute, allowing SQL injection.

Share product dividend listing concatenates user-controlled 'orderBy'/'sortOrder' values into the SQL and relies on ColumnValidator.validateSqlInjection(), which is bypassable with bare subqueries. This permits SQL injection through the share product dividend API.

Share account dividend listing concatenates user-controlled 'orderBy'/'sortOrder' parameters into SQL and validates only with ColumnValidator.validateSqlInjection(). Because that validation does not detect subqueries in ORDER BY, an attacker can inject arbitrary SQL expressions, enabling blind SQL injection.

Scheduler job history listing concatenates the user-controlled 'orderBy'/'sortOrder' values into SQL and validates them with the bypassable ColumnValidator.validateSqlInjection(). Bare subquery payloads in ORDER BY pass validation and are executed, allowing SQL injection via the scheduler jobs API.

Standing instruction history listing concatenates user-controlled 'orderBy'/'sortOrder' into SQL and validates only with ColumnValidator.validateSqlInjection(), which does not block subquery-based ORDER BY injection. An authenticated user can therefore inject arbitrary SQL expressions into the query.

Template mapper values are mustache-expanded and used as a URL that is fetched server-side (getMapFromUrl/getConnection). The URL whitelist check is only performed when 'fineract.template.regex-whitelist-enabled' is true, so by default an attacker able to create/edit a template can make Fineract issue arbitrary HTTP(S) requests (SSRF) to internal services. The connection additionally disables TLS verification via TrustModifier.relaxHostChecking(connection).

TrustModifier installs an all-trusting X509TrustManager and a HostnameVerifier that always returns true, then applies them to outbound HttpsURLConnection instances. This completely disables TLS certificate and hostname verification, making all such outbound requests susceptible to man-in-the-middle attacks. TrustModifier.relaxHostChecking is invoked from TemplateMergeServiceImpl.getConnection for template-based HTTP fetches.
